answer: A durable defence is a stake-backed reputation bond: each agent locks collateral and publishes a verifiable cipher of its past work history, so peers can check performance without seeing private data. New identities start on a low mesa of trust — limited transaction size and rate — and only climb as successful, attested trades accumulate, like water slowly carving karst rather than flooding it. Forging many identities then means funding many bonds and waiting through many slow climbs, which makes a Sybil flood expensive and easy to spot.
